title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' part of Grothendieck's continuation of La Longue Marche. He studies an extension 1 → 𝔊^+ → M_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1 (eq. (52)) and its 'natural' version M^♮_{ρ,σ}. Here ρ, σ are two 'points' or tangential data. The neighbouring pages fix the objects:
- N_ρ, N_σ are normaliser-type groups attached to ρ and σ.
- Z_{ρ,σ} is a centraliser-type group.
- G_{ρ,σ} is an ambient group, with embeddings i_Z, i_ρ, i_σ into it.
- Each of these maps to a common quotient γ_{ρ,σ}.
- Fibre products over γ_{ρ,σ} give So M^♮ = Z ×_γ N_ρ ×_γ N_σ ×_γ G and So Γ_{ρ,σ} = Z ×_γ N_ρ ×_γ N_σ.

On the previous page three subgroups of So M^♮ are cut out by U = i_Z(u), U = i_ρ(a), U = i_σ(b). Each maps isomorphically onto So Γ, so each is a section subgroup. This page pushes them down to M^♮_{ρ,σ}, whose elements are triples (a, b, U), giving (103):
- M[0] = {U ∈ Z_{ρ,σ}};
- M(ρ) = {U = a};
- M(σ) = {U = b}.

M(ρ) and M(σ) are sections of M^♮ → Γ^♮ = N_ρ^♮ ×_γ N_σ^♮. Given (a, b), the third coordinate is forced. Hence the semidirect ('½ directs') decompositions of (104) and (105):
- M^♮ ≃ M(ρ)·𝔊^♮ and M^♮ ≃ M(σ)·𝔊^♮;
- likewise M ≃ M(ρ)·𝔊^+ and M ≃ M(σ)·𝔊^+.

In each, the kernel 𝔊 is normal and M(ρ) or M(σ) is a complement.

The subgroup M[0] is not a section. It is an extension 1 → L_0^♮ → M[0] → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1, where L_0 is the kernel of Z → γ. Diagram (106) identifies this extension, via the isomorphisms with So M[0], with the extension So Γ_{ρ,σ}. That extension is the pullback of the extension 1 → L_0 → Z_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ} → 1 along the canonical map Γ_{ρ,σ} = N_ρ ×_γ N_σ → γ_{ρ,σ}.

The next page draws the consequence. A section of Γ_{ρ,σ} over γ_{ρ,σ} gives a section of M[0], and hence a third complement M(0), with M ≃ M(0)·𝔊. The purpose is to have explicit semidirect-product descriptions, i.e. choices of 'base point' complements, of the groups entering the loop equation.
errors: Equation number (103) is written over another number, apparently a 7…, and duplicates the label (103) already announced on the previous page. This is a minor numbering slip.
In (103), 'U = a' and 'U = b' abbreviate U = i_ρ(a) and U = i_σ(b). This is harmless.
No mathematical errors detected. The section and semidirect claims follow directly from the fibre-product definitions.

ideas.what: Section subgroups M(ρ), M(σ) of an extension, defined by the diagonal-type conditions U = i_ρ(a), U = i_σ(b), giving semidirect product splittings of M^♮ and M
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of a group extension / complement subgroup in a fibre-product (pullback) group

ideas.what: Identification of the extension M[0] of Γ_{ρ,σ} by L_0 with the pullback of the extension Z_{ρ,σ} of γ_{ρ,σ} by L_0 along Γ_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of group extensions (functoriality of extensions / H^2)

ideas.what: Several distinct 'base-point' complements (attached to ρ, to σ, and to 0 once a section of Γ over γ is chosen) of the same kernel in the loop-equation groups
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / different splittings of an outer action extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Grothendieck's Longue Marche (1981) for the general programme
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated) discusses related groupoid/base-point structures; this specific construction is unsure

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine bookkeeping of group extensions: section subgroups, semidirect decompositions and pullback of extensions inside a larger unpublished development. There is no new result or connection visible on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: The superscript rendered '§' throughout is ♮ ('natural'), as on the neighbouring pages: M^♮_{ρ,σ}, N^♮_ρ, Γ^♮_{ρ,σ}, L_0^♮.
'𝔖^§' / '𝔖^+' should be the Fraktur G, i.e. 𝔊^♮ and 𝔊^+, matching G^+ in exact sequence (52) on the previous page.
'sont des groupes relatives [?] au-dessus de' should read 'sont des (sous-)groupes sections au-dessus de'.
Final sentence: 'l'image inverse de l'extension Z_{ρ,σ} de γ_{ρ,σ} (lowercase gamma) par L_0^♮', not 'de Γ_{ρ,σ}'.
'via l'homomorphisme [?] canonique' reads 'via l'homomorphisme canonique', continued as (107) on the next page.

'D'autre part, on a un [?]' is followed by a struck or partly illegible word, probably 'diagramme'; the diagram's middle column shows So M_{ρ,σ}[0] mapping isomorphically up to M_{ρ,σ}[0] and down to So Γ_{ρ,σ}.
